overview: Chart and record rhyme most loudly around the open Heart / 'proving worth' theme: the client's own words — proof, report cards, invoices attached to love, a phone at 4% — map almost one-to-one onto that placement, and the record shows a live, dated trajectory of that belief loosening. Emotional authority and the 2/4 hermit-plus-network reading are quietly corroborated by the guilt-then-light, dread-for-nothing rhythm and the garden/alone-time entries. Where things diverge or stay thin: the chart's more determined patterns (open Spleen 'holding on', open Throat 'pushing to be heard') have only glancing support, and no resonance marks are recorded yet, so every chart-derived line here is a hypothesis to test with her, not a verdict.

components.title: Open Heart Center — 'Proving Worth'

beliefs.wording: Proof I've done something. Proof I'm worth the drive.
I just feel like a phone at 4%.
you don't have to be plugged in to something to deserve to be on

cautions: third parties who have not consented

crossRefs.theme: Worth must be earned through proof/achievement
crossRefs.connection: The client repeatedly narrates arriving to relationships and work with 'proof' and equates love with performance
crossRefs.validationQuestion: When you picture showing up somewhere with no 'proof' in hand, what do you notice in your body?

crossRefs.connection: Later entries show her testing arriving without proof and finding she is still received
crossRefs.validationQuestion: The dinner where you brought only yourself and a flan — what felt different afterward compared to the report-card visits?

components.traditional: An open (undefined) Heart center is classically described as someone who can feel a pull to prove their worth, to make promises and over-deliver, and to tie value to achievement — with the invitation being to notice worth is not something that must be earned.
homeworkIdeas: For one week, arrive to one interaction (a call, a visit) deliberately 'empty-handed' — no update, no accomplishment — and jot one line on what happened.
Notice and log each time the 'not-enough voice' speaks this week, plus how loud it was (1–10), building on her own 'smaller / I'm bigger' observation.
statementOptions: I am worthy exactly as I am, with nothing to show.
My worth is already true before I do anything.
I deserve to be here without earning it.

components.title: Open G Center — 'Unsafe To Be Seen' / identity through others

beliefs.wording: The garden is the only place I don't feel like I'm auditioning.
She's the only one I don't perform for.

crossRefs.theme: Identity felt as performance for others' eyes
crossRefs.connection: She describes 'auditioning', shrinking under a frown, and only feeling herself with the one person she doesn't perform for
crossRefs.validationQuestion: With Ana you say you don't perform — what is present in that relationship that lets you stop?

crossRefs.connection: The record shows approval-seeking clearly but says little about life-direction being outsourced specifically
crossRefs.validationQuestion: When you make a decision that's just yours, like the long walk home, how do you know it's the right direction for you?

components.traditional: An open G center is often described as sensing identity and direction through environment and other people, and can carry a felt sense of not being sure who one is unless reflected back — the growth edge being discernment about whose reflection to trust.
homeworkIdeas: Name three settings on a scale of 'auditioning' to 'just me', and pick one small way to bring a garden-like ease into one of them.
statementOptions: I am safe to be seen as myself.
I know who I am whether or not anyone reflects it back.

components.title: Open Sacral Center — 'When is enough enough'

beliefs.wording: I keep thinking if it's perfect enough then — then what? I don't finish that sentence
I am very good at finding urgent things when I don't want to feel.

crossRefs.theme: Overworking past the point of enough
crossRefs.connection: Repeated entries of staying late, redoing unrequested work, and saying yes reflexively
crossRefs.validationQuestion: What tells you a piece of work is 'done' — and whose voice sets that bar?

crossRefs.connection: Recent entries show her stopping at 'good enough' and leaving on time with the not-enough voice quieter
crossRefs.validationQuestion: Sending the third version and closing the laptop — what let you stop there?

components.traditional: An open Sacral is classically described as not having consistent life-force for sustained work and being prone to overdoing, pushing past healthy limits, and not knowing when enough is enough — often leading to burnout when the borrowed energy runs out.
homeworkIdeas: Set a 'first-version ships' experiment: choose one low-stakes task, send version one, and note what the not-enough voice says.
statementOptions: I recognize when I have done enough and I let myself stop.
Good enough is genuinely enough for me.

components.title: Emotional Authority — deciding through the wave

crossRefs.theme: Clarity/relief arrives after the emotional wave passes
crossRefs.connection: Decisions are followed by dread-then-fine, guilt-then-light, or shaking-then-relief
crossRefs.validationQuestion: When you told Andrés about Saturdays, how long before the dread turned into 'all that dread for nothing'?

crossRefs.theme: Deciding in the moment (against the wave)
crossRefs.connection: Saying yes before the sentence finished suggests in-the-moment agreement she later regrets
crossRefs.validationQuestion: What would change if 'let me sleep on it' were your default answer to any request?

components.traditional: Emotional authority is described as needing to ride an emotional wave over time before clarity arrives, rather than deciding in the moment — sleeping on things and noticing feelings settle before commitment.
homeworkIdeas: Practice one 'I'll get back to you tomorrow' response to a request this week and log the decision that emerged after the wait.
statementOptions: I give myself time to feel my way to clarity before I answer.
I trust the answer that arrives after I've slept on it.

components.title: Projector — waiting for the invitation & recognition

beliefs.wording: it felt good to be seen and not have to explain it away

crossRefs.connection: She describes chronic depletion and doing work nobody asked for
crossRefs.validationQuestion: Which of your efforts lately were actually invited, and which did you take on uninvited?

crossRefs.connection: Being truly seen by Ana and received by her father without performance felt nourishing
crossRefs.validationQuestion: What's the difference between being recognized and being praised for producing?

components.traditional: A Projector is described as gifted at seeing and guiding others but needing genuine recognition and invitation to thrive; without it, the classic signature is exhaustion and bitterness from over-giving in unrecognized effort.
homeworkIdeas: Track energy for a week: note when you felt seen/invited versus when you pushed uninvited, and how each left you feeling.
statementOptions: I let myself be recognized before I offer my energy.
My rest and my waiting are productive.
I thrive when I respond to genuine invitations.

components.title: 2/4 Profile — natural hermit within a network
cautions: third parties who have not consented

crossRefs.connection: Her clearest ease appears in solitary spaces — the garden, the headphone-free walk, Saturday mornings for herself
crossRefs.validationQuestion: How does the version of you in the garden differ from the version in the meeting room?

crossRefs.connection: Movement is catalyzed by named people — Ana, Valentina, testing 'no' out loud with others
crossRefs.validationQuestion: Who are the few people whose 'that's obvious' helps you see yourself more clearly?

components.traditional: A 2/4 profile blends a line-2 'hermit' who needs alone time to recharge and be called out for natural gifts, with a line-4 'opportunist' whose opportunities come through relationships and networks.
homeworkIdeas: Protect one recurring solitude window (like the Saturday mornings she already claimed) and note its effect on the week.
statementOptions: My time alone is where I come back to myself.
I honor my need for solitude without guilt.

components.title: Open Throat Center — 'Pushing to be heard'

beliefs.wording: My voice shook and I over-explained for a full minute
sorry, this is probably not what I'm supposed to write about

crossRefs.connection: She over-explains for a full minute, tags entries 'overexplaining', and peppers reflections with 'sorry'
crossRefs.validationQuestion: When you notice yourself over-explaining, what are you afraid will happen if you stop at the plain sentence?

components.traditional: An open Throat is often described as feeling pressure to speak or act to be noticed, sometimes talking too much or over-explaining to earn attention, with the invitation to speak when genuinely invited.
homeworkIdeas: Practice one 'no, thank you' with no reason attached, and record the urge to explain and what you did with it.
statementOptions: My 'no' is complete without explanation.
I am heard when I speak simply.

components.title: Gene Key 36 (Life's Work, Line 2) — turbulence to compassion

beliefs.wording: It's disorienting how much of my life I built to avoid a thing

crossRefs.connection: She narrates dread before events and a lifelong bracing for the world where 'saying no ends everything'
crossRefs.validationQuestion: That world you keep checking for and not finding — what would it free up if you stopped bracing for it?

crossRefs.theme: Turning toward feeling instead of away
crossRefs.connection: She experiments with sitting in the not-enough feeling rather than working it away
crossRefs.validationQuestion: When you managed four minutes with the feeling, what happened right before you reached for the 'urgent' email?

components.traditional: Gene Key 36 moves from a Shadow of Turbulence (dread and crisis-anticipation around new emotional experience) through the Gift of Humanity to the Siddhi of Compassion — often centering on how one meets emotional intensity rather than avoiding it.
homeworkIdeas: Extend the 'sit with the feeling' experiment by one minute at a time and log what shows up, without needing to fix it.
statementOptions: I can stay with a strong feeling and remain safe.
I meet my emotions with curiosity instead of avoidance.

components.title: Values Spiral — center of gravity in Drive

beliefs.wording: It doesn't need me to earn anything. It just grows or it doesn't and that's not a performance review.

crossRefs.connection: Work, deadlines, decks, promotions and productivity dominate the earlier record
crossRefs.validationQuestion: What would 'success' feel like if it weren't measured by output?

crossRefs.connection: The garden, the walk, and 'best hour of the week' point toward a quieter, flow-based value gaining weight
crossRefs.validationQuestion: Where in your week do you already feel 'flow' rather than 'drive', and how could there be a little more of it?

components.traditional: A center of gravity in 'Drive' describes a person oriented toward achievement, results, and forward momentum — energized by goals and outcomes, with an emerging pull noted toward Achievement and Flow.
homeworkIdeas: Once this week, choose an activity purely because it feels good (not because it produces anything) and note how it lands.
statementOptions: I value my presence as much as my productivity.
I let ease count as a worthy way to spend my time.
